headline: Stevens Cross Country
transcription:
The Stevens Cross Country Team opened up its season last Saturday at the Wagner Invitational. For the first time in many years it didn't rain at the first meet.

Stevens defeated NJIT by one point. Co-captain Greg Morriello led the way with a time of 31:05 for the five-mile course. The top five runners were Brian Hampeys, Steve Kostakis, Vince Bienfait, and Alex.

Coach Al Alonso was pleased with the race performance but was displeased with several unnamed runners for eating behind a bush in the warm down run.

For the first time, Stevens had a girls team. Tara, Marlie, and Silvia displayed good potential for the girls' 3.1 mile course. Any girls interested in joining the team should show up on Wednesdays at 4:00 p.m. in front of the Walker Gym.

The next meet is this Saturday at 12:00 noon at Kings College.

headline: Thinclads Rained On Again
transcription:
The Kings Invitational was run last Saturday and once again, it rained. The cross-country Ducks defeated NJIT for the second time in a row, although the NJIT coach said "Our best runners did not show-up."

Greg Morriello led the way for the men with a time of 31:06. Following Greg were Steve Kostakis, 32:42, Alex Gomez, 33:26, Vince Bienfiet and Lou Coless. Tara Master and Marlie had good showings for the women. Look for the Duck Thinclads to give it their all against NJ Tech tomorrow at Garrett Mountain.

transcription: In their first dual meet of the year, the cross country team lost to NJIT 32-25. Coach Al Alonso attributed a "hard training week" and "off days" by some of the runners as reasons for the loss. For the Ducks, junior Greg Moriello finished first. Shah, a junior, cut 2 minutes off his previous time to place tenth. For the women, freshman Tara Master, placed first with a time of 22:59.

headline: Cross Country Team Finishes 5-3
meet_or_event: dual meet vs. Polytechnic; Ramapo Invitational
transcription: The Stevens cross country team continued their success, when they won their last two dual meets to end their season with a 5-3 record. It was the tenth straight season that the team has finished at least at .500 for the year. In the meet on Sunday against Polytechnic, senior Greg Moriello, led the way, with a time of 31.09. Finishing fourth overall was junior, Steve Kostakis, with a time of 32:44. Junior Brian Hampeys placed third for Stevens at 33:04. Saturday at the Ramapo invitational, Moriello finished with a time of 28:47, ninth overall, and Hampeys was behind him at 31:08, good for 16th. Coach Al Alonso praised Hampeys and junior, Nanik Khemlani for their solid runs over the weekend. Freshman, Tara Master finished first for the women at the Ramapo invitational. She came in with a time of 22:32, second overall.

headline: Cross Country Teams Open Eleventh Season
transcription:
Coach Al Alonso has "a strong nucleus of experienced runners" returning to begin the 11th season on Saturday, September 14th at the Wagner Invitational.

Leading the team again will be senior Greg Moriello. He holds seven Stevens records and has been in the top three finishers for Stevens 20 times since 1988. Moriello placed first in every event, and was honored by the New Jersey "9", an independent Athletic Conference last year.

Also back from last year's team are seniors Steve Kostakis and Lou Coless. Kostakis had five second place finishes last year. He ws also honored by the NJ "9". Newcomers Derek Cholon, Kenn Armstrong, and Morgan Samuels are all runners to look out for this season.

There will also be six women running for Stevens, although they don't have an official status. The two to watch out for are sophomore Tara Master and junior Nancy Wu. Master came in second at the NJ "9" and Ramapo Invitational events last year.

headline: New Faces Lead Thinclads
transcription:
Cross country participated in it's first meet this past week in the Wagner Invitational. The Ducks were sparked by strong performances from two freshmen, making the future look bright for the Stevens thinclads.

Competing in a field that included Division I and II opponents, freshman Derek Cholon was the first Stevens runner to finish, completing the race in 31:30.

Following Cholon across the finish line was freshman newcomer Scott Streichenwein, who finished in 32:35. Shortly thereafter, seniors Steve Kostakis and Lou Coless finished third and fourth for the Ducks with the times of 33:18 and 34:55 respectively. Rounding off the top five for Stevens was transfer student Kenn Armstrong, finishing in 35:35.

In the womens 3.1 mile race, three Ducks performed admirably. Sophomore Tara Master led the Stevens ladies across the finish line in a time of 24:41. Junior Nancy Wu's 25:22 placed her second for Stevens while freshman Linda Geoghegan placed third in 27:12.

Al Alonso, coach of the thinclads, was pleased with how the team performed in it's first outing. Looking forward to a good season, he stated "Our times compare favorably with what we did a year ago."

headline: Steven's Runners on the Move
transcription:
The Stevens cross country runners put their skills to the test again this past week at the Kings Invitational. Once again the Ducks had a good outing.

Leading the pack for Stevens for the second straight week was freshman Derek Cholon. He finished in 30:32, which placed him thirty-sixth out of the 80 runners.

Close behind Cholon for the Stevens thinclads was senior Greg Moriello, who finished in a time of 31:36. This placed him forty-second in the field.

In third and fourth for the Ducks were senior Steve Kostakis at 32:18 and freshman Scott Streichenwein at 32:30. The afternoon's big surprise, however, was senior Chik Li. He was able to cut three minutes off his previous time on the Kings course in an impressive run.

For the women, junior Nancy Wu set the pace for Stevens at 24:50. Following her across the finish line were sophomore Tara Master at 26:10 and junior Tanya Acosta at 31:25.

With his team getting into top shape, Coach Al Alonso is pleased. He commented "It was a pretty good outing for us". The Ducks will run next at Van Cortlandt Park in the Hunter Invitational on Saturday, September 28.

headline: Cross Country Off and Running
transcription:
Saturday, September 28 saw the Ducks running in the Hunter Invitational at Van Cortland Park. Once more the Stevens harriers ran well.

For the third straight week, freshman Derek Cholon led the Ducks across the finish line in an impressive time of 29:47. Following the rookie were seniors Greg Moriello, finishing in 31:11, Chik Li at 32:40, Steve Kostakis at 33:13, and Lou Coless just a few strides behind, finishing in 33:19. Sophomore Jim O'Neill rounded out the top six for the Ducks, finishing the circuit in 36:52.

On the ladies side, junior Nancy Wu ran impressively, finishing in 26:50, earning her the honor of athlete of the week. Freshman Linda Geoghegan followed Wu across the finish line.

Coach Al Alonso has been preparing his runners for their first dual competition of the fall this Sunday when Stevens will take on CCNY at Van Cortlandt Park. States coach Alonso, "Right now, we're doing okay. With the depth we have I've been able to rotate people every week. That could pay off later in the season."

headline: First Dual Meet Goes Well For X-Country Ducks

transcription:
Last Sunday, Stevens ran in it's first dual meet competition at Van Cortlandt Park. Coach Al Alonso said of his team, "We're starting to fall into form".

Eight schools ran in the event, one of which was Stevens. The Ducks were victorious over five of their opponents while losing to only two. For the specific schools and scores, check the Stevens Scoreboard.

For the fourth straight week, freshman Derek Cholon led the Ducks across the finish line in a time of 30:36, placing him fifth overall. The next runner across the finish line, in sixth place, was Duck freshman Anton Musto at 31:10. Musto's effort was a pleasant surprise and earned him the honor of being named Athlete of the Week.

Senior Greg Moriello was the next Stevens runner to finish, in a time of 31:38, good for fifteenth. Soon thereafter, freshman Scott Streichenwein finished, placing seventeenth overall.

Three ladies represented Stevens in the women's race. Junior Nancy Wu paced the Ducks in 26:04 placing her tenth overall. Sophomore Tara Master finished in 27:37, good for fifteenth while freshman Linda Geoghegan finished eighteenth in a time of 28:29.

headline: Thinclads Top The NJ "9"
meet_or_event: New Jersey "9" Championship at Drew (Loantaka Brook Park); IAC Championship at Garrett Mountain
transcription:
On Saturday, October 12, the Stevens thinclads ran in the New Jersey "9" Championship hosted by Drew at the 5 mile Loantaka Brook Park circuit. The Ducks took the competition, winning the New Jersey "9" championship.

Once again the Ducks were led by none other than Derek Cholon in what proved to be his best performance thus far. Cholon ran a 28:15, just eight seconds off the Stevens record of 28:07 set by Mike Tamkutonis in 1988. Cholon's time was good enough to place him first for the Ducks and fourth in the overall competition. It also earned him the honor of being named athlete of the week.

Senior Greg Moriello followed Cholon across the finish line at 30:40, placing him fifth overall. Freshman Anton Musto finished seventh overall at 31:07. For this performance Musto received honorable mention from the NJ "9". Senior Jack Li rounded out the top finishers for the Ducks in a time of 31:42, good for eighth overall.

Reflecting upon his team's performance, Coach Al Alonso commented "It was an outstanding performance for us. I needed one-hundred percent from everybody and I got it." Looking forward to Sunday's IAC title race, Alonso stated "We'll need the same type of effort next Sunday."

In the women's race, it was sophomore Tara Master leading the Ducks with a time of 23:19, placing her ninth in the field. Junior Nancy Wu and freshman Linda Geoghegan also ran well, placing tenth and fifteenth respectively.

Sunday, October 20 saw the Ducks chasing the IAC title at Garret Mountain. The Ducks took second place in the field of seven with a total of 46 points, only beaten by NJIT's 32 points.

Freshmen Derek Cholon and Anton Musto paced the Ducks, finishing sixth and seventh respectively in the field. Freshman Scott Streichenwein, who garnered praise from Coach Al Alonso, finished twelfth overall despite being troubled by injuries. Seniors Jack Li and Steve Kostakis gave it their all in rounding out the placing Ducks, finishing eleventh and fifteenth in the field. Kostakis' consistency has pleased Alonso.

headline: Men's & Women's Cross Country Begins
transcription:
Last week the men's and women's cross-country teams started a new campaign at the Wagner Invitational. The men's team, who sported three freshmen, finished in tenth place overall while the women's team placed in fourteenth overall.

The men's team is shooting for their twelfth consecutive winning season under ninth year coach Al Alonso. Last year, the ducks won the Jersey "9" title with seven wins and two losses. The team is anchored by the strong sophomore combination of Derek Cholon and Anton Musto. Cholon finished first in all eight events in 1991 while Musto was in the top three on five different occasions. Both runners were recognized by the IAC for their feats of excellence.

The women's team, on the other hand, is making its intercollegiate varsity debut. This enthusiastic and hardworking group of runners is led by senior Nancy Wu and junior Tara Master, who holds five Stevens records in her two year career. Sophomore Linda Geoghegan and senior Silvia Pinel are also expected to be competitive. A close eye must also be kept on newcomers Eugenia Kowalski and Janet Smith who could provide some pleasant surprises this fall.

Both teams are expecting to be competitive this fall utilizing all of the talent that has found its way to the Stevens campus.

headline: Men's Harriers Win and (Get) Lost
meet_or_event: dual meets vs. John Jay, Mt. St. Vincent, York, Polytechnic, CCNY and Pratt; Drew meet at Loantaka Park
transcription:
A Couple of weeks ago, the Stevens men's cross country team had an outstanding run winning five of six trackmeets. They beat the likes of John Jay, 23-34, Mt. St. Vincent, 19-42, York, 16-47, Polytechnic, 23-36, and CCNY, 20-35. They did, however, lose to Pratt, 20-43.

Sophomore runner Derek Cholon paced Stevens in the five victories that opened dual meet competition. He was timed at 32:01 that placed him in third overall. Freshman Dan Dalfonzo came in eighth with an impressive clocking of 34:23. Gustavo Brandt, also a freshman, came in thirteenth overall with a time of 36:31.

This great run assured coach Al Alonso's team its twelfth straight winning campaign.

Last week, however, along with Drew's runners, the Stevens men's cross country team seemed to get a little bit off course at Loantaka Park. In fact, neither team scored five thinclads and it was scored as an incomplete meet for both "lost" squads.

"Some of our harriers followed Drew's people and they all got mixed up," said coach Alonso.

Sophomore Derek Cholon and freshman Dan Dalfonzo did finish the course, however. Cholon paced Stevens with a 31:16 clocking placing third overall while Dalfonzo placed sixth with a 34:23 clocking.
summary: Stevens won five of six dual meets to clinch a twelfth consecutive winning season, then had a meet at Loantaka Park scored incomplete after runners from both Stevens and Drew went off course.

headline: Men's, Women's Cross Country Do Well
transcription:
Last week, the Stevens men's cross country team performed well at two key meets — the Jersey "9" Championship and the Drew Invitational. The male ducks came in second at the Jersey "9" championship while placing fifth at the Drew meet. Coach Al Alonso's team was paced by three harriers in both meets. Freshman Dan Dalfonzo clocked in at 33:24 coming in eighth and 32nd for each meet, respectively. Another freshman, Gustavo Brandt, timed in at 34:07 placing ninth and 36th. Senior Chik Li was clocked at 35:08 finishing tenth and 37th.

The women's team also fared well at these same meets last week. The lady harriers came in third at the Jersey "9" championship and fifth at the Drew Invitational. Freshman Eugenia Kowalski led with her Stevens record-breaking time of 21:39 that gave her fifth overall place at the Jersey "9" race. This feat is even more extraordinary since she was coming off of a serious injury. She followed this strong performance by finishing 13th at the Drew Invitational. Also pacing Stevens was senior Nancy Wu who ran a 22:22, placing tenth at the Jersey "9" meet. She also came in tenth at the Drew meet.

The men's and women's cross country teams will again be in simultaneous competition at the Ramapo Invitational on Saturday. The men's team will run solo at Van Cortlandt Park against Yeshiva on Sunday.

headline: Men's, Women's Cross Country Finish Strong
meet_or_event: IAC Championship; Ramapo Invitational; first annual Halloween Classic at Van Cortlandt Park
transcription:
The male harriers ended their successful campaign with a very busy week participating in three events in that span. On Wednesday, Stevens came in fourth at the IAC Championship. Sophomore Derek Cholon led the way placing eleventh with a 33:26 clocking.

On the next Saturday at the Ramapo Invitational, Freshmen Dan Dalfonzo and Gustavo Brandt did well. Dalfonzo placed 20th with a 33.11 time while Brandt immediately followed at 21 with a 33:56 time. Coach Al Alonso himself came in fifth with a 29:17 clocking as a thinclad in the open division.

At the first annual Halloween Classic, sponsored by Stevens, Polytechnic and Yeshiva at Van Cortlandt Park. Cholon placed second, at 31:44, while Dalfonzo placed sixth, at 35:25. In their last meet, Stevens beat NJIT and Yeshiva to finish its tenth winning season in twelve years. They finished the fall season with a sterling 7-1 record.

The women participated in two events last week and fared well. At the Ramapo Invitational, Stevens was led by freshman Eugenia Kowalski, fifth, clocking in at 23:15, and senior Nancy Wu, eighth, clocking in at 23:50.

The very next day at the Halloween Classic, Wu ran a 40:44 while Kowalski finished at 41:17. These two meets were joint efforts along with their male counterparts. All in all, the lady harriers finished at 3-1 in their first varsity season ever.
summary: Stevens closed the 1992 season with the men 7-1 and fourth at the IAC Championship, and the women 3-1 in their first varsity season; coach Al Alonso himself ran the Ramapo open division.

headline: Harriers Show in Jersey "9" Championships
transcription:
The Stevens harriers competed in the combined Drew Invitational and Jersey "9" Championships this past week. The men finished well, taking fourth place in the Drew Invitational and third place in the Jersey "9" competition. The women also placed well in the Jersey "9" championships, finishing third in the competition. The lady harriers did not fare so well in the Drew Invitational, finishing in sixth place.

Steve Kropac continued to pace the Tech runners. For the third time this season Kropac was the first Duck across the finish line with a time of 28 minutes and 30 seconds. This time earned him a second place finish overall in both events. Gustavo Brandt followed closely behind to finish with a time of 34 minutes and 23 seconds. Nick Cabrera also placed for the men's harriers. The men's cross country record is currently 3-1.

The lady harriers were led by a familiar trio. Eugenia Kowalski finished the course with a time of 22 minutes and 39 seconds. With a time of 27 minutes and 5 seconds, Tanvi Pandya finished the course second. She was followed 2 minutes later by Silvia Pinel. The women's team is 1-2 at this time.

The harriers' efforts led to positive results this past week. Coach Alonso stated, "We're coming along and pointing toward the IAC championships." And with this goal the Tech cross country runners continue to train until the Bard Invitational on the 23rd of October.

headline: Kropac Bests All at Van Cortlandt Park
meet_or_event: IAC Championship and Halloween Classic at Van Cortlandt Park
transcription:
The Stevens men's cross country team finished out their year last Sunday at Van Cortlandt Park. Sunday, October 31st, was the combined run for the IAC championship and the Halloween Classic.

On Stevens home course Steve Kropac managed a time of 29:49 for the hilly five mile course. This time gave Kropac first place in both races. Kropac was only the second runner in Stevens history to do so. With the help of Kropac's strong finish Stevens managed a fourth place finish in the team competition for the IAC championships (out of 7 schools). In the Halloween Classic the Stevens men placed fourth out of ten schools.

The women's team also performed well. Eugenia Kowalski finished with a time of 24:27 in the women's division. This time earned Kowalski a second place finish overall.

When asked about the performance of the Stevens Harriers coach Al Alonso said, "I was pleased with our performance in the IAC Championship." On this note the cross country season ended for Stevens.

headline: Stevens XC Runner Goes to ECAC
meet_or_event: ECAC Cross Country Championships at Tufts University
transcription:
This years cross country team sent an excellent runner to the ECAC cross country championships. After a long, hard season of running, Steve Kropac was honored with a bid to participate in the ECAC championships last Saturday.

Kropac ran consistently well all season with times near 28-29 minutes for most of the season. The ECAC would be his best performance yet. Kropac set a personal and season best with a time of 28:10 on the course at Tufts University. Despite this excellent time, Kropac finished only 79th out of 262 runners.

Kropac and the rest of the team are finished for the year. A season wrap-up will be included in next week's issue.

transcription:
The IAC Championship and the Halloween Classic were held on Sunday, October 30, at Van Cortlandt Park. Both the Men's and Women's Cross Country teams placed high with great times, putting the Ducks far ahead of the competition.

Running is not just a simple trot; it requires the use of muscles, the mind, and the determination of the heart. Freshman Leslie Tyrie, of the Women's Cross Country, demonstrated those three qualities and her exceptional endurance as she captured the IAC Individual Championship with an impressive time of twenty-four minutes and forty-six seconds and named Athlete of the Week. Placing third was teammate Sheila Moya, sophomore, with a time of 32:32.

The Men's Cross Country team was not far behind as sophomore Steve Kropac captured third pace in the IAC Championship with a time of 30:14. Advancing close behind was senior Vic Wynnytsky, timed at 31:22, which put him in sixth place. In the Halloween Classic, Wynnytsky placed seventh, followed by sophomore Mark Vido at 14th, timed at 32:29, and freshman Nirav Patel, 32:56, good for fifteenth.

This Sunday, both teams will be competing again at Van Cortlandt park against Yeshiva and Polytechnic.

headline: Men's Cross Country Team at ECAC Championships
transcription:
The ECAC Championships was hosted last weekend by SUNY-Albany. Sophomore Steve Kropac distinguished himself as usual, placing fiftieth of 187 with an outstanding time of twenty-seven minutes and forty-five seconds. Senior Vic Wynnytsky placed 141st with a time of 30:29 and Freshman Nirav Patel placed 157th with a time of 31:49.

Coach Al Alonso is pleased with the team's performance, especially with that of Kropac's. He stated that all of his runners did well, adding, "I knew Kropac had it in him to get below 28:00." Kropac, in his second year running for Stevens, placed first in fifteen straight events, making his efforts and endurance admirable.

Patel, a newcomer to the squad, feels that it was a privilege to have been exposed to the entire athletic aspect of Stevens. He believes that cross-country consists of much training and dedication—half physical and half mental—and attributes the success of the team to the commitment of their coach. He stated, "Coach Alonso stayed for two workout sessions a night, sacrificing his evenings and nights for over a month. What other coach would do that for such few people?"

The Men's Cross Country team holds a very impressive record. They placed second at the Independent Athletic Conference meet and the Halloween Invitational and placed third at the Wagner Invitational and the Drew College Invitational.

This weekend, heading into the end of the season, both the Men's and Women's Cross Country teams will compete at the NCAA Mid East Regionals at Allentown College in Pennsylvania. We wish them the best of fortune!

headline: Track Team Can't Stop Breaking Record: Seven This Week
transcription:
The Stevens Institute of Technology Track & Field team competed at William Paterson College during the weekend. Not only did they have another outstanding outing, but continued to break school record after record against three Division I and eight Division III teams.

Coach Adalberto Alonso set a school record in 1981 which was unmercifully broken by sophomore Steve Kropac last weekend when he took 8th place in the 5000m run in 16:22.9, making him second to finish among the eight Division III teams. Kropac did not let it end there, as he took fifth place in the Sprint Medley in a time of 3:55.7, another record. Others competing in the event were freshman Almasi Glenn, sophomore Rich Defreitas and junior Tony Bayule. Kropac went on to finish sixth in the Distance Medley in a record time of 12:29.9 in which also competed sophomore Nicolas Cabrera, freshman Thorsten Roberts and sophomore Brian Ribnicky.

In other events, Gisufu Gibson broke a record which he had set, taking third in the discus with a throw of 114'10". Gibson also took third place in javelin, 164'0". Paul Dener took seventh place in both the shot put, 35'4", and the discus, 95'7.5". Sophomore Harold Dean took second place in the high jump, tying a school record of 6'2". Dean, Bayule, Defreitas and Glenn comprised the 4x100m team, taking fourth place with a time of 48.4 while freshmen John Waka, Luis Rodriguez, Alistair Henry and Thorsten Roberts finished seventh in 49.8.

The women were also very successful with freshman Kendred Wilson, sophomore Joanna Welenc, freshman Leslie Tyrie and senior Lucy Kim. They were able to place first in the Distance Medley with a time of 16:43.8 and fourth in the Sprint Medley, 5:19.5, breaking two more school records.

The Track & Field team will have competed at Yale University and the York Invitational before the weekend is over.

headline: Cross Country Teams Begin Season Impressively
meet_or_event: Wagner Invitational (Staten Island) and Vassar Invitational
transcription:
The Men's and Women's Cross Country teams opened their season on September 9th at the Wagner Invitational in Staten Island, NY against NCAA Division II and III teams. The men's team finished in second place with excellent performances by captain Steve Kropac (29:52), freshman Dave Donohue (31:13), sophomore Jose Tapia (32:08), freshman Jakuba Miles (32:40), freshman Andres Sulling (33:33), freshman Patrick Gregorio (33:34), sophomore Martin Jakubowski (36:39), freshman Robert Kinney (37:29), junior Brian Ribnicky (38:30) and senior Javier Dela Cruz. This was their highest finish at this meet to date. Coach Alonso was very pleased with everyone's times, especially since the top 6 runners were all faster than last year's 3rd man.

The women's team finished in a tie for 3rd with Ramapo College behind the record breaking performance of freshman Seema Dixit. With a time of 22:53, she broke the old record set by team captain Leslie Tyrie. Junior Joanna Welenc finished in 24:40, running almost five minutes faster than her last time on this course! Freshmen Mildred Santos, 27:37, Harmony Semf, 29:07, Annette Arena, 38:55, and Hina Ahmad, 39:04, also had impressive performances. This was Arena and Ahmad's first race ever and Coach Alonso was very pleased to see that they were able to make a contribution to the team so quickly. Coach Alonso feels that both of these teams, men and women's, will go down in the record books for fastest 5-person averages by the end of the season.

This past weekend, the team traveled to the Vassar Invitational and again had another outstanding showing. The men's team took second among twelve teams, the previous highest finish being fifth, and the women's team took fourth among thirteen teams, just two points behind third and significantly better than last year's eighth place finish. Steve Kropac holds the new school record of 28:15 as he finished fourth. Close behind Kropac was Donohue who placed eleventh, setting a freshman school record of 29:56. The rest of the pack consisted of Miles in thirteenth place with 30:24, Sulling in sixteenth with 30:35, Gregorio in eighteenth with 30:59, Tapia in twenty-second with 31:45, Kinney in thirty-first with 33:41, Jakubowski in fortieth with 35:26 and Ribnicky in forty-first with 35:54. The women were led by Dixit finishing fourth and breaking the school record with a time of 20:30. She was followed by Welenc in twentieth with 22:39, whose time was also under the previous school record. Santos finished thirtieth in 24:31, Semf was in thirty-second place with 25:17 and Arena was forty-fourth in 29:25.

The teams travel to Van Cortlandt Park this weekend and are looking to improve on last year's perfect 5-0 record. CCNY will probably be their toughest competition. The women will be looking to regain their winning record which they lost last year. The teams have been practicing very hard and the results are showing; everyone's times are dropping weekly. Coach Alonso feels that with the addition of freshman Rebecca Flanagan, who has been having difficult with her asthma due to the higher levels of pollution in the NYC area, the women's team will be surprising many.

This weekend is very important for both teams and could really use a cheering crowd to lead them to victory. Come out and support our teams, this meet will be exciting.

headline: Cross Country Shows Strength

transcription:

headline: Cross Country in the Lead
transcription:
The Stevens Institute of Technology Men's Cross Country team traveled to Madison this past weekend to compete in the Drew Invitational. headline: Men's X-Country Places Second at Bard Invitational
meet_or_event: Bard Invitational; upcoming IAC / Halloween Invitational
transcription:
The men's cross country team placed second among nine teams at the Bard Invitational this past weekend. Since 1993, Steve Kropac has led the way for the Ducks and made it his twenty-fourth time over the weekend. In the midst of all the rain and slippery conditions, Kropac crossed the finish line in 29:11, giving him his second championship of the season. Second place for Stevens and ninth overall was freshman Dave Donohue with a time of 32:02.

Both sophomore Jose Tapia and freshman Yakubu Miles ran the event in 33:41, placing 15th and 16th while Pat Gregorio was dashing towards the finish line with a final time of 36:16, placing 29th among the 65 runners. The rest of the crew consisted of Greg Quinn who finished 34th (38:15), Mike Quinn in 45th (43:18), and Pete Dewes in 50th (47:32).

The Men's and Women's Cross Country teams will be competing in the IAC/Halloween Invitational this weekend. This may very well be the most important event of the season, according to Coach Al Alonso. Stevens and NY Maritime are the top contenders for the IAC crown and each has had an upset over the other this past season. There is no question that everyone on the team must perform at 100% in order to win. They really could use all of the support and loyal cheering of as many classmates as possible. All you Ducks out there should attend this last event, you won't be disappointed.

headline: X-Country Competes in Halloween Classic and IAC Tourney

transcription:
The men's cross country team traveled to Van Cortlandt Park to compete in both the Halloween Classic and the IAC Championship. The thinclads placed second out of sixteen teams in both events, which are run simultaneously. They took second place out of seven in the IAC Championship and second of ten in the Halloween Classic.

Jose Tapia came in fourth for the IAC, four seconds behind Kropac. Freshman Yankuba Miles placed fifth (30:00) and fellow freshman Dave Donohue placed sixth (30:02). The fifth Stevens runner to cross the finish line was freshman Patrick Gregorio, taking 16th place with a time of 31:51. Although Stevens placed four runner in the top six spots, defending champion, NY Maritime, took the IAC title.

Others runners consisted of Robert Kinnet in nineteenth (33:36), Martin Jakubowski in twenty-first (34:05), Greg Quinn in 35th (35:12), Mark Samson (36:09), Pete Dewes (37:40) and Mike Quinn (39:11).

Other key runners included freshmen Harmony Semf (6th-26:40), Mildred Santos (8th-27:49), and Annette Arena (10th-29:20). headline: Cross Country Review
transcription:
The men's cross country team ended the season with a perfect 7-0 dual meet record and had excellent showing at eight other events. The team has an overall record of 78-31 in fifteen years and has raised its dual meet streak to twelve.

Coach Adalberto Alonso is proud of the accomplishments made by his team. He stated that the freshman quickly adapted to running the five miles required in college cross country as opposed to three in high school. In addition, he pointed out, "Our top five averaged 29:03, second best in our history."

Junior Steve Kropac led the way for the team in eleven events, breaking a record for the most firsts for a season in the IAC, and broke a number of records at the Institute. Kropac holds a career total of twenty-eight first place finishes for Stevens, also and IAC record. Kropac broke the Vassar Invitation record with a time of 28:15, the record at Van Cortlandt Park with a time of 28:24 and the Bard Invitational record with a time of 29:11. Freshman Dave Donohue and sophomore Jose Tapia placed second four times for Stevens, in addition, Tapia placed third five times. Sophomore Yakuba Miles also made a great impression on his coach, finishing in the top three seven times.

Kropac, Tapia, Miles and Donohue were named All IAC while Coach Adalberto Alonso was named IAC Coach of the Year.

The women's cross country team had the best dual meet record since the establishment of the team in 1992, 4-1. Freshman Seema Dixit placed first for Stevens at eight events and set three career re-cords at the Institute. Dixit set the Wagner Invitational record with a time of 28:54, the Vassar Invitational record with 20:30, and the record at Van Cortlandt Park with a time of 22:09. Junior Joanna Welenc accumulated a total eight second place finishes, improving last year's times by two to five minutes.

With increased experience, Coach Alonso feels that the teams will have an outstanding season next year and can improve on their already impressive performance.
summary: A 1995 season review: the men went 7-0 in dual meets with Kropac setting an IAC record for most first-place finishes in a season, four runners named All-IAC, and Adalberto Alonso named IAC Coach of the Year; the women posted their best dual meet record since the team's 1992 founding.
notability_note: Kropac set IAC records for most first-place finishes in a season and a career (28), broke three course records, and four Stevens men were named All-IAC; Alonso was IAC Coach of the Year. Dixit set three career records at the Institute as a freshman.

headline: Stevens Competes at Madison
transcription:
The Stevens Track and Field Club traveled away to Madison to compete in the annual Drew Invitational this past Sunday. Among the competitors, the team played against William Paterson, and Drew. These teams knew of Stevens' success in track during the spring, but did not anticipate the whole team being there. Usually during the Winter track season, the majority of schools have skeleton teams.

The Ducks placed in almost every event. Steve Kropac ('97) lead the way by winning the 1500 meter and 3000 meter runs by almost half a lap. Kropac later anchored the 4x400 relay team into a 3rd place finish. Paul Redner ('97) won the shot-put with a throw of 37'8", while Yankuba Njie ('99) took the 400 meter run with a time of 55.9 seconds. Njie also placed 3rd in the 55 meter dash, placing with a time of 6.6 seconds, followed by Matthew Brown ('98) finishing in 6.6, Fred Mansell ('99) in 6.8, and Tafari O'Mealley ('99) in 7.1.

Kameelah Majied took 2nd place in the Women's 55m event, placing a school record of 8.1 seconds. She later came back with a 3rd place performance in the 200m, finishing with a time of 31.2 seconds. In the men's 200 meter race, Brown took 4th place with 25.3 seconds, followed by Mansell, with a 26.8, O'Mealley with a 27.1, and Njie with a 27.8

In the pole vault, Sven Northcott ('99) and Patrick Panico ('99) placed first and second in the pole vault with heights of 12'0" and 8'0" respectively. The final event of the day, was the 1600 meter run. In it, Brown, Njie, and Yakubu Miles ('99), and Kropac exchanged batons for a time of 3:52.4.

Overall, the team placed six points behind Columbia, one behind St. Peters, and three ahead of Division I team CW Post.

headline: Track Athlete of the Semester
meet_or_event: Athletes of the Season series; NCAA Regionals (upcoming)
transcription:
Steve Kropac ('97) is the first athlete to be featured the Athletes of the Season series. Kropac is from Manalapan, New Jersey and dedicates a great deal of time to his passion — running. He is a transfer student from Rochester Institute of Technology, a Division I school. To keep up his pace, Steve runs fifty-five to seventy miles a week, depending on the weather conditions and does weight training three times a week.

Track & field and cross country coach Adalberto Alonso is proud of Kropac's accomplishments. In fact, Kropac has broken a good number of cross country records which Coach Alonso himself set during his years at the institute. Included among his accomplishments are running the Van Cortland Park course in 28:24, one second under Alonso's time. Kropac also broke the Wagner Invitational record at Stevens, a 5.2 mile course, with a time of 29:15 and the Vassar Invitational record at Stevens in 28:10.

As far as Track & Field is concerned, Kropac has set the following Stevens records: 800m in 2:01, 1500m in 4:03.7, 3000m in 9:27, 5000m in 16:22 and the Steeple Chase in 10:20. Kropac's performance in the 1500m last Sunday qualifies him for the NCAA Regionals to be held on May 11, which is the last regular season competition.

Kropac's best finishes for Stevens include 30th place in the 1994 NCAA Mid-East at Allentown College and 42nd place in the 1995 ECAC at Williams. Steve feels that his goal for track is to crack the 4:00 barrier in the 1500m. For cross country in the fall, he aspires to finish in the top twenty-five at the NCAA regionals and make the nationals.

Cross country teammate Mark Sanson commented, "Steve does excellent job in both cross country and track. He deserves success through his year-long dedication. He always competes with himself because even when he wins, he wants to do better." Coach Alonso remarked, "Steve's accomplishments demonstrate that anything can be accomplished through hard work and dedication."

Tech Athletics congratulates Steve Kropac on his true athletic spirit!

headline: Cross Country Team Gets Ready for Season
transcription:
The men's cross country team is ready to open its season this Saturday, September 14 at the Wagner Invitational. The runners were 7-0 in dual meet competition last season, with their top runners returning for another year of competition they are hoping to go undefeated. The team has never had a losing season in its 15 years at the Institute and has posted a 78-31 record in duals. Coach Adalberto Alonso is very excited, "We have a very solid group of returnees and I like three of our new runners. I'm pleased with our training progress so far. I expect us to do at least as well as we did last fall."

The key runner and captain this year is again Senior Steve Kropac. Kropac has twelve career records at Stevens, breaking a number of the records set by his coach while he was an undergraduate. He came in first place for Stevens at all eleven events last season, totaling 28 straight 1st place finishes for the school in three years. The coach feels that Kropac is destined to have another great year and finish off an impressive career.

Also returning are Sophomores Yakubu Miles, Dave Donohue and Juniors Jose Tapia and Nirav Patel. Newcomers include Freshmen David A. Bakos, Chris Naiva and Andy Cole, all with high school experience.

The women's team will also be at the Wagner Invitational on Saturday. The ladies were 4-1 in duals last season. Returning is last year's key runner, Sophomore Seema Dixit, who as All IAC in 1995 had a best time of 20:30 at the Vassar course. Also returning are Senior Joanna Welenc, Junior Sheila Moya and Sophomores Mildred Santos and Harmony Semf. Joining the team this are sophomores Rebecca Flanagan, Daniella Kranjac and Freshmen Minita Patel and Winnie Yau.

headline: Cross Country Places Well
transcription:
Both the men's and women's cross country teams participated in the Wagner Invitational this last week. The men's team made a respectable showing despite Clove Lake's odd course rearrangement, which caused some of the runners to make some unnecessary detours. Leading the team was senior Steve Kropac, who ran with a time of 29:19 to finish sixth overall.

The women's team, was led by Freshman Minita Patel, who ran the course with a finishing time of 23:00, giving her a nineteenth place college debut. Sophomores registered the rest of the point for Stevens, with Daniella Kranjac, Harmony Semf, and Mildred Santos with finishing times of 27:04, 28:09, and 29:10. headline: Men's and Women's Cross Country
transcription:
The Vassar Invitational Cross Country race was a day of improvement, injury and college debuts as well as a solid finish for the Stevens Cross Country Team. The women's cross country team, finishing 8th out of 14 in the team scoring, contributed to this feat by running faster this week than last. Freshman Minita Patel finished first for Stevens, coming in at 21:42, which was an improvement over last week and was good enough for 26th overall, out of a field of 87 runners. Running close behind were sophomores Harmony Semf and Daniella Kranjac. Semf was most impressive on the field of Stevens runners as she crossed the line at 25:39 which was over 2 minutes faster than her time last week of 28:09. At the same time she earned Athlete of the Week honors. Kranjac made her college debut with an impressive time, clocking in at 25:28. Closing out the finishers were freshman Wing-Yin Yau at 27:41 and senior Stephanie Dennis at 30:08. Unfortunately the day did not end on a high note, with the misfortune of one of our runners being injured. Sophomore Mildred Santos took an unfortunate fall before the first mile mark and may be on the injured list for a while. However, the improvements of her teammates made up for her misfortune. Overall, the women ran well, and they hope to improve in their next race at CCNY.

On the men's team, there was also room for improvement. The team finished 4th out of 13 teams. In a field of 78 runners, Senior Steve Kropac crossed the tape in 28:18 to finish first for Stevens. At the same time he was a mere three seconds off of his 1995 school record. Kropac blazed to 9th place overall. Not far behind was sophomore Yakubu Miles , who blitzed to a 29:34, shaving a minute off of his time from last week. In 1995, Miles was clocked at 30:34. Finishing off this impressive day came freshmen Chris Naiva at 30:34 and Dave Bakos at 31:19, who finished 24th and 34th overall; and to complete the scoring was Sophomore Dave Donohue in at 33:11. Naiva and Bakos cut their times substantially in comparison to last week. According to Miles, "The team did very well overall. Although we are missing some of our key runners, we fared well. When they return, our team should be more than solid."
summary: At the Vassar Invitational the Stevens men placed 4th of 13 and the women 8th of 14, with Kropac running 28:18 — three seconds off his own school record — and Harmony Semf cutting over two minutes from her previous week.

This past Sunday at Van Cortlandt Park, senior Joanna Welenc led her team to an 5-3 finish in the team scoring, crossing the line in 25:44. She also finished 14th overall in the field of runners. headline: Cross Country Improves
meet_or_event: New Jersey State Championships; Drew Invitational
transcription:
This past week was one of improvements, firsts, and a solid finish, for the women's cross country team. Sophomore Harmony Semf finished first for the Ducks. This was a day to remember for Semf as it was the first time that she led the pack for Stevens. She finished in tenth place overall with 26:24.

Sophomore Rebecca Flanagan came in just under ten seconds later at 26:35. Finishing up for Stevens were freshman Wing-Yin Yau at 33:25 and junior Claudia Gomez at 33:49. Their record stands at 5-3, as the Drew Invitational was a non-scoring meet.

Making their first appearance at the New Jersey State Championships was not just a challenge but also a reward for the Men's Cross Country team, who, at the conclusion of the day, finished third out of eight in a very competitive field of Division III teams.

"It was a very challenging course with a big bowl or loop and a lot of hilly trails," noted Coach Al Alonso. "Overall we did okay." That okay performance included senior Steve Kropac's 32nd in a row first place finish for Stevens with a running time of 28:44. Kropac's endurance was good enough for a 44th place finish out of 110 competitive runners. Less than two minutes later came Freshman Yakubu Miles, blazing across the finish line in 30:06. The steadfast improvements of this runner earned him 65th place. The field was completed by freshmen Chris Naiva, Dave Donohue, and anchor man Dave Bakos. They arrived in 31:05, 32:43, and 33:00 respectively.

The next day, at the Drew Invitational, the men's team again sought ways to improve. Kropac finished fourth overall at 28:37, with Naiva closely behind at 30:37 for 20th place. Bakos shaved over two minutes off Saturday's time, with 31:12 for 28th overall. Freshman Andy Cole and Donohue completed the scoring for Stevens in 33:08 and 33:13. The 8-0 Ducks are looking for good things to happen at their next meet at the Stevens Invitational at Liberty State Park.

headline: Cross Country
meet_or_event: Stevens Invitational at Liberty State Park
transcription:
Stevens hosted its first invitational meet at Liberty State Park in Jersey City. The Men's team placed third in a field of eleven in the team scoring. Senior Steve Kropac, holder of an unprecedented 34 consecutive first-place finishes, added one more to his collection. Not far behind was sophomore Yakubu Miles, with a time of 28:56. His speed earned him an impressive 11th place overall. Following Miles was freshman Chris Naiva coming in at 29:43 for 16th overall. Completing the field were freshman Andy Cole and sophomore Dave Donohue hitting the line at 31:44 and 33:00. Their performances earned them 23rd and 26th overall. The Men's team is taking a two week break as they prepare for the IAC Championship on October 27.

The Women's Cross Country took a satisfying fourth out of nine in the team competition at the Stevens Invitational this past week. Freshman Minita Patel crossed the tape first, with an impressive time of 22:28. Her time earned her a ninth place finish in a field of 45 runners. Senior Joanna Welenc finished second with a 24:30. Her speed earned her a 17th place overall. Daniella Kranjac came six seconds later, with a 24:36 and an 18th place finish. Finishing 23rd overall came sophomore Harmony Semf with a time of 25:57. The field was completed by sophomore Rebecca Flanagan crossing the line at 27:02, for 27th overall.

The women's team continues to improve as they hold on their 5-3 overall team record. It is evident that the ladies are working hard, as Athlete of the Week Kranjac ran much faster than her last outing. There are no meets scheduled for this week for the Women's team, but we encourage them to look ahead until the end of the season.
summary: Stevens hosted its invitational at Liberty State Park, where the men took third of eleven and the women fourth of nine, and Kropac notched his 35th consecutive first-place finish for the school.

headline: Kropac Places 1st at IAC X-Country Championships
meet_or_event: IAC Championship and Halloween Classic at Van Cortlandt Park
transcription:
Steve Kropac, Stevens Cross Country runner placed first at the IAC Championship held at Van Cortlandt Park. Timed at 28:49, Kropac increased his number of first place finishes to 35. This is his second individual IAC crown, his first coming in 1993. Other Stevens runners finishing in the top ten include Sophomore Yakubu Miles placing fifth in 29:45 and freshman Chris Naiva placing sixth with a time of 30:01.

At the Halloween Classic, the women's varsity Cross Country team placed second overall out of a field of nine teams. Sophomore Harmony Semf finished the race with a time of 25:09, and placed second in the IAC event. Freshman Minita Patel came in with a time of 25:38 to finish third in the IAC Championship. Sophomore Daniella Kranjac had a 27:08 time to place third for Stevens in all three events and fifth in the IAC race. Both teams compete in the ECAC Championships at the University of Massachusetts, Dartmouth on November 2.

headline: Cross Country Competes at ECAC Championships
meet_or_event: ECAC Championships; dual meet at Van Cortlandt Park
transcription:
The Men's cross country team had an impressive showing at the ECAC Championships, coming in 15th of 43 teams. "We're on a cloud," commented coach Adalberto Alonso. Senior Steve Kropac blazed the field with an very impressive time of 26:37. Kropac finished 28th overall in a field of 218. This was his best time ever. Following him was sophomore Yakubu Miles who completed the course with a 27:55. Three seconds behind was freshman Chris Naiva at 27:58. Freshman Dave Bakos and sophomore Dave Donohue completed the scoring, coming in at 30:03 and 30:08 respectively. The Men's team had almost all of their runners under the 30 minute mark.

The Men's team found themselves running remarkably well the next day at Van Cortlandt Park. Steve Kropac set a course record with a time of 27:45. And also extended his first place victory streak for Stevens to 37 straight. Kropac was first in the entire field of runners. "This was my best race ever," said Yakubu Miles who ran a personal best of 29:06 on this hilly course. Miles' time earned him 4th overall. Following close behind was Chris Naiva with a 29:20, who improves tremendously with each race. Finishing up for Stevens came Andy Cole, 32:13, and Dave Bakos, 32:30. Athletes of the Week are Steve Kropac, Yakubu Miles and Chris Naiva. This weekend the team goes to the NCAA Mid-East Regionals.

The Women's Cross Country team had a decent showing at the ECAC Championship. Sophomore Harmony Semf came in first for Stevens with a personal best of 23:07. "I did not realize how fast I was running," said Semf, "but I was very happy with my time." Athlete of the Week Semf finished 158th out of 201. Sophomore Mildred Santos, junior Claudia Gomez, and freshman Wing-Yin Yau also put in great efforts for the women's team. The team has struggled for a consistent number of women at each race. This weekend they will attend the NCAA Mid-East Regionals.
summary: Stevens placed 15th of 43 at the ECAC Championships with Kropac running a career-best 26:37, then set a Van Cortlandt course record of 27:45 the next day to extend his streak to 37.

headline: Women's Cross Country Ends Season at Mid-East Regionals
transcription:
The women's cross country ended their season with a fine showing at the NCAA Mid-East Regionals. Scoring a team finish of 36th out of 43 teams, these women proved themselves able to withstand the pressure of the Division I runners. Freshman Minita Patel set a course record for Stevens as the women sent a full team to the NCAA event. Patel crossed the line at 24:28, earning 216th place. Sophomore Harmony Semf finished 219th, clocking in at 24:44. Senior Joanna Welenc repeated her 1995 time of 25:24 to place 227th. The field was completed by sophomore Mildred Santos and freshman Wing-Yin Yau, with times of 27:23 and 27:47, respectively. The women finished their dual meets with a record of 5-3. This was last race for senior captain Joanna Welenc.

A season of streaks, defeats, injury, and triumph came to an end as the men's cross country team competed at the NCAA Mid-East Regionals. For the first time in his Stevens career, sophomore Yakubu Miles finished first for Stevens. Miles crossed the line in 28:58, placing 118th in a field of 251 runners. "The course was muddy from the rain and we were truly worn out from last week's back-to-back races," commented Miles. Completing his rookie season was freshman Chris Naiva, who followed Miles with an impressive 29:11. This season has to be a satisfying one for Naiva, who ran consistently throughout. He is sure to be an instrumental part of the team next season. This was the end of a remarkable streak for senior Steve Kropac. After achieving 37 first place finishes for Stevens, Kropac hopes to leave a mark for others to follow. Kropac was clocked at 29:28, placing 139th. Finishing up the scoring was sophomore Dave Donohue, 30:24, and freshmen Dave Bakos, 32:04, and Andy Cole, 32:14. The men's team finished with a dual meet record of 12-0.

headline: Cross Country Wins Halloween Classic, Still Undefeated

transcription: By Lou Villanueva. The women's varsity cross country team went into the ECAC championships last week with one primary goal - to defeat Ramapo College. The opposition had defeated the Ducks in the WIAC championships earlier in the year. Stevens edged ahead of Ramapo to place 20th out of a total of 34 teams in the women's field. A total of 148 runners competed on the women's side. Finishing first for the Ducks was freshman Maureen Amador, who placed 86th overall with a time of 21:27. Following behind her, in second place for Stevens, was sophomore Yelena Havryliuk, who finished in 98th place with a time of 21:48. Rounding out the top three for the women was sophomore Natalie Vanatta. Vanatta finished in 134th with a time of 22:37. For the men, the team finished in 24th place overall among a total of 33 competing teams. Out of a field of 239 runners, senior Yakubu Miles placed first for the Ducks once again, placing 61st overall with a time of 28:34. In second for Stevens was sophomore Chris Naiva with a time of 29:40.1, coming in 121st overall. In third for Stevens was sophomore Dave Bakos, who finished 154th with a time of 30:27. Coach Alonso commented, "I was really proud of the women's performance. We set out to beat Ramapo and then made it happen. In addition, finishing 20th in this meet is pretty good when you consider that we were competing against some of the strongest teams in the northeast. The men also ran well and finished just behind Ramapo. The guys have been working extremely hard and it shows in their times. I'm looking forward to seeing further improvement in the NCAA's."

headline: Cross Country Closes out Season
transcription: By Hannah Davies. At the NCAA East Regional, both the men's and women's cross country teams finished their respective seasons. Both squads made respectable showings, with the women finishing 27th out of 50 teams present, and the men coming 33rd out of the 50 teams. The women's squad finished their season with an overall record of 8-0. The men closed out their season with a record of 11-0. The women had one of their strongest seasons in the history of the program, and finished it out with a strong performance on Saturday. Freshman Maureen Amador, who finished first for Stevens in each race this year, led the way in 109th place at 21:28. Sophomore Yelena Havryliuk finished right behind Amador in 21:30. The next four runners for Stevens were sophomore Natalie Vanatta in 187th place at 22:56; freshman Rebecca Dougherty in 213th place at 23:35; senior Mildred Santos in 242nd place at 24:44; and sophomore Anne Krone finished in 270th place with a time of 27:01. As for the men, senior Yakubu Miles closed out a fine career and an outstanding season by running his fastest race yet on the Allentown course in 27:32, good enough for 64th place. Junior Chris Naiva finished his finest season to date by crossing the finish line in 29:14 and 133rd place. Gabriel Miani set a Stevens freshman record for the Allentown course in 30:07, finishing 198th place. The next three finishers for Stevens were senior Greg Quinn in 30:59 (221st); Sachi Desai, 32:47 (249th); and junior Andrew Cole 33:05 (252nd place). "A lot of our runners improved their time from the Allentown Invitational, which was one of our main goals going into this competition," remarked Coach Al Alonso. "I thought Mildred, Yakubu, and Greg all finished their careers in fine fashion; they've been great role models for our younger team members."

headline: Track & Field Breaks 17 School Records
transcription: By Lou Villanueva. On February 13-14, the Stevens track and field team participated in the CTC Championships at Southern Connecticut State University in New Haven, Connecticut. The men placed 9 out of 17 teams competing. Sophomore Patrick Bastien placed second in the 400-meter dash with a time of 51.44 seconds. Bastien earned an automatic qualification for the ECAC Championship to be held the first weekend of March and ran well against some top ranking Division I, II and III teams. In the 55-meter dash, sophomores Kevin Frei and Brian Williams ran times of 6.78 and 7.13 seconds respectively, placing seventh and 20th in the field of runners. Frei also came back to place fifth in the 200-meter dash while setting a school record of 23.55 seconds. Williams followed closely behind placing among the strong field of runners. Sophomore Andrew DeLiso ran the 400-meter dash placing in the top twenty. DeLiso also captured 6th place in the 55-meter high hurdles with a time of 8.70 seconds. Next, senior veteran Yakubu Miles ran a time of 1:14 in the 500-meter dash, placing ninth. Miles later returned to capture third place in the 1000-meter run. Juniors Tom Zapata and Greg Quinn rounded out the distance races by running in the 800-meter dash and mile run, respectively. In the field events, junior Sven Northcott captured the bronze (third place finish) in the men's pole vault, tying a school record with a 12'6" mark. The men's 4x400 relay saw DeLiso, Miles, Frei, and Bastien placing fourth with a time of 3:37.21. The women's team placed 10 out of 17 teams competing. The 55-meter dash concluded with a sixth and eighth place finish by juniors Efe Kragha (8.07 seconds, school record) and Kameelah S. Majied (8.31 seconds). Kragha continued her sprinting efforts with a school record of 29.46 seconds in the 200-meter dash, good enough for eighth place overall. Junior Kameelah S. Majied scored ninth place overall in the 400-meter dash. Majied's effort was a school record coming in at 1:09.19 seconds. Freshman Maureen Amador made strides in the 500 (1:36.27 seconds) and 1000-meter (3:25.89 seconds) dashes coming in 12th, with sixth place overall. Amador's performances were school and freshman records. Senior Mildred Santos had a noteworthy performance in the 1500 meter walk-race, which not only earned her a seventh place overall finish, but a new school record. Running also for the women were the distance medley relay team consisting of senior Seema Dixit, sophomore Winnie Yau, and sophomore Laura Monchinski. The relay team's effort earned them a sixth place overall finish in a new school record of 15:36.06 seconds. For the 4x800-meter relay, Amador, Dixit, Santos, and Yau paired up for a seventh place finish. The women's team also had noteworthy performances in the field events of the two-day championship meet. Efe Kragha and freshman Hillary Green combined efforts and scored second and fourth place finishes in the high jump. Their leaps of 1.42 meters earned them a shared school effort record. Once again, Kragha excelled in the long jump with an overall eighth place finish with a leap of 4.56 meters. Junior Kameelah S. Majied and Kragha added efforts in the triple jump and shot put, respectively. Maureen Amador rounded out the points with a school record in pole vault, on her first attempt. A select group of athletes will make a last attempt at qualifying for the prestigious ECAC Championships this weekend at the MAC Championships at the Armory in New York City; while the rest of the team continues training for the first home meet on March 20 at the Annual Stevens Invitational to be held at Secaucus High School.

headline: Track and Field Ready for Season
transcription: By Lou Villanueva. Coach Al Alonso and both his men's and women's varsity track teams are ready to compete for their second season of varsity competition. With the combination of returning players, and a pack of newcomers, the team looks to improve on the success they had in their first year of competition. For the men, Stevens has a slew of talent. In the cross-country department, the Ducks' lead men will be senior co-captain Yakubu Miles. Miles has been one of the top runners in the history of Stevens, and will be helped along with the talents of juniors Dave Bakos and Greg Quinn, and freshman Gabriel Miani. For sprints, look for sophomore Patrick Bastien to compete well. Bastien had a decent season indoors, and looks to reach national qualifying times this spring. Also contributing in sprints will be junior co-captain Fred Mansell. Mansell was a finalist in the Collegiate Track Championships in the 100 meters last year, and although has had to deal with injury, should compete well. In hurdles, the Ducks have sophomore Andrew DeLiso, and two members from the men's basketball team. Senior Almasi Glenn and freshman Jeff Houser will both compete in both the hurdles and jumping events. After having a successful season in the pole vault indoors, junior Sven Northcott looks to perform well outdoors, along with competing in the decathlon. In throwing events, look for sophomore Ernest Buechel to perform well in the javelin, along with the other throw events. For the women, the talent for the distance events comes from the cross-country team as well. After having a good rookie season, freshman Maureen Amador looks to make a solid contribution to the track team. Joining her will be sophomore Laura Monchinski and seniors Mildred Santos, Seema Dixit, junior Winnie Yau, and freshman Michelle Devlin. For sprints, the Lady Ducks will have junior co-captain Efe Kragha, who performs well in sprints, jumps and throws. Kragha will concentrate on shorter sprints. Other stronger sprinters include Yau and junior Kameelah Majied, and freshman Rebecca Dougherty. Dougherty will also help in hurdles, while freshman Hillary Green will help Kragha and Majied in the jumping events. Senior LeTisha Shaw and Kragha will also contribute well in the throwing events. Coach Alonso commented, "Both teams are pretty well balanced. We are building our depth and have more talent than a year ago. The main goal is for both teams to improve their finishes in each meet in comparison to last year and I don't see any reason why that won't happen."

headline: Cross Country Finishes Well in ECAC Championships
transcription: By Hannah Davies. This past weekend both the men's and women's cross country teams competed in the ECAC Championships. Miani has finished first for the Ducks in seven of the eight of the races in which he has run this year. Senior Tom Zapata, also turned in his fastest time of 1999 by finishing the course in 31:01.57/154th place. Senior Greg Quinn, 31:05.45/158th place; sophomore Sachi Desai, 31:39.01/173rd; and freshman Wayne Fontaine, 32:09.35/184th rounded out the top five for the Ducks. The women also finished well with an overall finish of twenty-second out of the 35 teams competing. Senior Yelena Havryliuk turned in her fastest ECAC time in her four year career with a 21:44.01/75th place. Junior Laura Monchinski ran her fastest time of the year, 22:00.53, which was good enough for 91st place. Sophomore Rebecca Dougherty followed Monchinski in 145th place/23:21.30. The fourth and fifth finishers for Stevens were Michelle Devlin, 186th place/24:39.88, and Melissa McAvoy, 194th/24:56.85. This weekend the men and women compete in the NCAA Regional Championships.
